name: ARC-MOF carbon-capture material selection
description: select_mofs(descriptors, operating_conditions, observations, budget) -> list of unused integer MOF indices. Observations reveal computed working_capacity_mol_kg and selectivity. One query per call, maximum twenty queries. Score highest observed capacity meeting the operating-condition selectivity constraint divided by the pool optimum. Topology/chemistry groups remain disjoint and target-derived descriptors are forbidden.

sources.locator: Structures, adsorption outputs and chemistry/topology clusters.

sources.title: Discovering Ultra-Stable Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Capture from A Wet Flue Gas: Integrating Machine Learning and Molecular Simulation
sources.locator: Screens ARC-MOF materials for carbon capture using learned filtering and molecular simulations. The local dry post-combustion VSA working-capacity replay, selectivity constraint and query budget are narrower and do not reproduce wet-flue-gas stability screening.

requirements.datasets: Pinned ARC-MOF process and geometry source tables339MB, --arcmof preparation builds512 materials in four128-material pools for post-combustion VSA.

limitations: Independent SCIEL adaptation of a cited scientific problem; no claim to reproduce author leaderboard scores.
Candidate and evaluator run in one Python process; data access is separated by API, not an OS sandbox. Isolate evaluator data for adversarial or held-out evaluation.
Bounded zero-shot post-combustion VSA replay; selectivity>=10 is a local design constraint. No cross-topology or unseen-chemistry transfer claim.
Only target-free released geometry descriptors are candidate inputs. Source mmol/g working capacity equals mol/kg numerically.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Identify metal-organic frameworks with useful carbon-dioxide separation performance.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Selective CO2 capture materials are candidates for lowering the energy and resource costs of emissions control.

papers.title: Discovering Ultra-Stable Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Capture from A Wet Flue Gas: Integrating Machine Learning and Molecular Simulation
papers.primary_goal: Identify stable MOF adsorbents with favorable CO2 capture properties under flue-gas conditions.
papers.task_relation: The paper searches ARC-MOF materials for carbon capture. The local finite-pool task optimizes working capacity subject to selectivity under its own operating conditions; it does not test the paper's wet-gas stability claims, full process economics or experimental deployment.
